To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the effects of NMDA antagonist drugs on a working memory delayed conditional discrimination task in rats can be explained by a reduction in discriminative ability and not by a reduction in the ability to remember.
NMDA receptor antagonists impair working memory in rats.
NMDA receptor/channel antagonists produce a reduction in discriminable stimulus information, but do not affect rate of forgetting in a delayed conditional discrimination task.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new class of anticonvulsant drugs.
the development of a new approach to understanding the relationship between memory, attention, and consciousness.
understanding the neural mechanisms of learning, memory and attention in the rat and human.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NMDA antagonism disrupts delayed conditional discrimination.
these results suggest that NMDA receptor/channel antagonists impair delayed conditional discrimination by disrupting stimulus discriminability.

the NMDA receptor/channel antagonists CPP and/or MK-801 have no effect on the rate of forgetting, but do have a linear dose-dependent effect on stimulus discriminability in a delayed conditional discrimination task.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NMDA receptor/channel antagonists, MK-801 and CPP, impair delayed conditional discrimination.
NMDA receptor/channel antagonists disrupt working memory and that this disruption is due to a reduction in the ability to discriminate between stimuli.

the NMDA antagonist CPP, in the doses used here, disrupts delayed conditional discrimination by reducing stimulus discriminability and does so by a process that involves a disruption of the hippocampus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NMDA antagonism can disrupt delayed conditional discrimination in a manner similar to the disruption of working memory in the radial arm maze.
the delayed conditional discrimination task may provide a sensitive index of NMDA-mediated processes in working memory.
the effects of NMDA antagonist on working memory can be dissociated into effects on stimulus discriminability versus effects on rate of forgetting.
